meaning unsettled DATA LogProjectile.MinDistance rolling MinDistance 2500 millitiles = 45000 subtiles distance; meaning unsettled DATA LogProjectileRolling.MinDistance airborne Gravity 30 unknown (arc parameter) DATA LogProjectile.Gravity cast delay if the airborne phase covers MinDistance 10 ticks = 0.500 s (k=15) or 8.33 ticks = 0.417 s (k=18) ticks / seconds from deploy to rolling hitbox at the tap INFERENCE 54000 / (360*k) roll duration 2018 range: 66.6 ticks = 3.33 s (k=15) or 55.5 ticks = 2.775 s (k=18); live range: 3.03 s or 2.525 s ticks at TICK_MS=50 / seconds INFERENCE ProjectileRange / (200*k)

Behaviour, in order

  1. PLACEMENT [DATA spells_other.Log.SpellAsDeploy=true with CanDeployOnEnemySide blank, versus Tornado SpellAsDeploy=true AND CanDeployOnEnemySide=true and Miner (troop) CanDeployOnEnemySide=true -- cross-card: SpellAsDeploy switches to troop placement, CanDeployOnEnemySide lifts it; COMMUNITY fandom The_Log 'It can only be deployed on the player's own side', trivia '1 of 3 spells which can only be placed in the player's own territory']: territory = the TROOP rule (Territory::OwnHalfAndPocket, same pocket depth key as troops). Not Territory::Anywhere.

  2. PLACEMENT, river exception [COMMUNITY fandom 2018-04-25 'allowed The Log to be placed on the river if a Crown Tower has been already destroyed']: when the enemy princess of a lane is destroyed, the river (water) half-cells of that lane are legal for the Log; otherwise water -> DeployError::Water as for troops. Which river cells exactly is unsettled (see unsettled).

  3. PLACEMENT, buildings [DATA CanPlaceOnBuildings=TRUE; COMMUNITY 2017-03-13 bug 'not able to be deployed on top of buildings', fixed 2017-06-12]: no Occupied/footprint check. Whether the tilemap NO_DEPLOY bits (king block, river-corner tiles) block the Log is unsettled.

  4. DEPLOY: elixir 2 deducted and the card cycles exactly as for any card (existing state.rs deploy_slot). No deploy time (spells_other.Log.CustomDeployTime blank) [DATA].

  5. AIRBORNE PHASE [DATA LogProjectile has no Damage; COMMUNITY AesDragon 'still in the air without a hitbox ... 360']: a non-entity projectile that deals no damage, pushes nothing, cannot be hit. Default launch model (calibration key spells.SPELL_AS_DEPLOY_LAUNCH_MODEL=airborne_from_behind_lands_on_tap): starts MinDistance (54000 subtiles) behind the tap along the team-forward axis, moves at 360*k subtiles/tick with the last step clamped, and on arrival spawns the rolling projectile AT the tap [INFERENCE; the Barbarian Barrel river lore and the Goblin Barrel counter lore both need the roll to cover tap .. tap+ProjectileRange].

  6. ROLLING DIRECTION [INFERENCE; the Log cannot be aimed]: straight along the team-forward axis, +y for Blue and -y for Red (engine mirror (x, 32-y)). Never homing (Homing blank). Not clamped to the arena bounds (Monk trivia: a deflected Log leaves the arena) [INFERENCE].

  7. ROLLING MOTION [DATA ProjectileRange, Speed]: each tick in Phase::Projectile advance by 200*k subtiles, clamping the final step so total travel from the roll start is exactly ProjectileRange (199800 in 2018 data, 181800 live); then despawn (DeathEffect log_die is visual only).

  8. HIT TEST each tick [INFERENCE for the shape, see unsettled]: a swept axis-aligned rectangle x in [x0-35100, x0+35100], forward extent [prev-10800, cur+10800] (team frame), against each victim's collision circle edge-to-edge (the same edge convention as combat::splash). Swept so the result does not depend on TICK_MS. This geometry must live in fixed.rs, the only place distance arithmetic is defined, integer, i64 squares.

  9. VICTIM FILTER [DATA OnlyEnemies=true, AoeToGround=true, AoeToAir blank; COMMUNITY]: enemy team only (no friendly fire); ground entities only (flying never hit); alive; not already hit by THIS log (a per-projectile hit set, so each entity is hit at most once -- fandom Barbarian_Barrel 'The Log which will only hit the tank once'); deploying units ARE valid victims (fandom 'Any swarms placed on top of The Log will be immediately hit', and the Goblin Barrel counter lore); hidden Tesla is NOT a victim (fandom Tesla: immune to everything but Earthquake/Freeze while underground, live); units mid-jump are NOT victims (fandom: Hog Rider, Mega Knight, Ram Rider, Royal Hogs 'cannot be struck by it while they use their jump abilities'; the engine has no jump yet).

  10. DAMAGE [DATA]: level-scaled Damage (card level through rarities.Legendary, truncating) pushed into the DamageBuffer. Crown towers (King and Princess) take damage*crown_pct/100 through combat::damage_against. Other buildings (Cannon, Tesla) take full damage. Applied in Phase::Resolve with every other hit, so simultaneous logs from both sides stay order-independent. A King Tower hit with amount > 0 wakes the king through the existing resolve() king_hit path.

  11. KNOCKBACK [DATA Pushback, PushbackAll; COMMUNITY]: every TROOP victim hit this tick (not buildings, not towers), INCLUDING IgnorePushback=true units (Giant, Prince, Baby Dragon is air so never hit), gets a knockback of Pushback subtiles. Record it in a push buffer during Phase::Projectile and apply it after Resolve to victims that survived, summing buffered displacements so the order cannot matter. Default direction (calibration key knockback.DIRECTION_ROLLING=radial_from_projectile_centre): the unit vector from the log's current centre to the victim, in integer arithmetic. This is INFERENCE, chosen because three fandom strategy lines need a sideways component: lane switching by 'deploying The Log on the side of the troop opposite', pushing troops 'closer to the inside of the Arena', and pushing a corner Miner 'towards the King's Tower'. A pure forward push cannot produce any of the three.

  12. KNOCKBACK SIDE EFFECTS [COMMUNITY fandom The_Log]: 'If a troop is locked into a target, the pushback caused by The Log will reset their attack animation' -- set attack_phase out of Windup and restart the load timer. Keep or drop the target lock: unsettled. Once Charge exists, knockback also cancels the Prince's charge [COMMUNITY 2016-09-19]. A unit on the river edge can be pushed 'over the river back to the opponent's side' [COMMUNITY], so knockback is NOT blocked by water the way walking is; how it resolves is unsettled.

  13. END: the rolling projectile despawns after ProjectileRange. The rule 'at most once per victim' holds for its whole life, and nothing re-hits.

Targets affected. Enemy ground troops, including units still deploying, take full damage and knockback. Knockback also moves IgnorePushback units, because PushbackAll=true. Enemy non-tower buildings take full damage and no knockback. Enemy crown towers (King and Princess) take damage x CrownTowerDamagePercent (40% in 2018 data, 13% live) and no knockback; a hit on the King Tower activates it. Air units are never hit. Friendly units are never hit (OnlyEnemies=true, no friendly fire). A hidden Tesla (live) and units mid-jump are not hit. Each entity is hit at most once per Log.

Unsettled

  • LAUNCH MODEL / CAST DELAY (LogProjectile.MinDistance=3000, Gravity=30). Candidates: (A) the airborne log starts MinDistance behind the tap and lands on the tap, then rolls tap..tap+ProjectileRange, giving a 0.5 s (k=15) or 0.417 s (k=18) delay before any hit; (B) airborne from the tap forward MinDistance, with the roll ending at tap+ProjectileRange, so nothing between the tap and tap+3 tiles is ever hit; (C) the roll starts at the tap instantly. Evidence: Barbarian Barrel 'placed at most 2 tiles from the river, the Barbarian will spawn at the opposing side' (live range 4.5) rules out 'airborne forward, then a full ProjectileRange roll' but does not separate A from B; 'swarms placed on top of The Log will be immediately hit' and 'Log placed on the centre tile behind the Tower always hits all 3 Goblins' favour A or C over B. crforge implements B with a units bug its own comment admits. DECIDING OBSERVATION: 60 fps recording of a Log dropped with a Skeleton exactly on the tap tile and a second Skeleton 1.5 tiles ahead. Note (i) whether the tap-tile skeleton is hit, and (ii) the frames from release to the first damage number.
  • ROLLING MinDistance=2500. Candidates: (a) ignored whenever ProjectileRange is set; (b) a no-hit zone for the first 2.5 tiles of the roll (crforge). This contradicts the swarm-on-top lore unless the roll starts well ahead of the tap, and would make the live Barbarian Barrel (range 4.5) miss everything in its first 2.5 tiles; (c) a minimum travel distance for non-rolling use. DECIDING OBSERVATION: the same recording as above. Under (b) a Skeleton 1 tile ahead of the tap survives.
  • HIT SHAPE. Candidates: rectangle vs victim circle edge-to-edge (a Knight of radius 0.5 is hit out to 2.45 tiles off-axis), or the victim centre inside the rectangle (hit only to 1.95 tiles). 2023-03-27 'improved The Log's collision detection' changed something unspecified, so the live shape may differ from 2018. DECIDING OBSERVATION: Skeletons at 2.2 tiles lateral offset from the log centre line on both sides; hit under edge-to-edge, untouched under centre-in-rectangle.
  • KNOCKBACK DIRECTION. Candidates: radial from the log's centre point (default; matches the lateral-push lore), travel direction only (crforge; contradicts the lore), or perpendicular from the nearest point of the log's centre segment (pure forward for |dx|<=1.95, so no lane switching). DECIDING OBSERVATION: track a Knight struck 1.5 tiles off-axis; its displacement vector is diagonal under radial and pure-y under travel-direction.
  • KNOCKBACK PROFILE AND MASS. No column or global gives a duration or a mass law (globals.csv has no PUSHBACK key; Mass is not a formula). Candidates: instantaneous teleport vs linear slide over N ms; distance independent of Mass vs mass-scaled. DECIDING OBSERVATION: Log a Skeleton (mass 1) and a Giant (mass 18) side by side; compare total displacement and the number of frames the slide takes.
  • KNOCKBACK INTO WATER, BUILDINGS, UNITS. The river-crossing lore says water does not stop the push. Candidates: allow the overlap and then resolve to the nearest bank (possibly the far bank), or clamp at the bank; building footprints could block the push or resolve it afterwards. DECIDING OBSERVATION: Log a Knight standing on the bridge exit and one at a river bank next to water.
  • ATTACK RESET DETAILS. 'Reset their attack animation' is certain (COMMUNITY). Unknown: whether the target lock survives, and whether LOGIC_LOAD_FIRST_HIT_RESET_TIMER_AFTER_ATTACK-style load-first-hit timers reset too. DECIDING OBSERVATION: a Knight hitting a tower is logged; measure the frames from the push to his next hit, compared with load_time and hit_speed.
  • SPEED DIVISOR FOR PROJECTILES. The engine and card.rs:57 apply the troop multiplier (UNVERIFIED). The claimed split 'troops /50, projectiles /60' traced to no source: crforge and legacy/ use /60 for both; the only frame measurement found (fandom Darknighture 2023) gives x1.2 (/50) for both troops (Giant) and projectiles (Musketeer). DECIDING OBSERVATION: live Log roll time, first contact to despawn, is 3.03 s at /60 and 2.525 s at /50.
  • NO_DEPLOY CELLS AND RIVER CELLS FOR THE LOG. Can it be placed on own king-tower no-deploy block and the river-corner tiles (0,14)/(17,14)? After a lane's princess falls, which river half-cells are allowed (lane half only, or the whole river)? DECIDING OBSERVATION: drag the Log over each in a friendly battle and note the placement indicator colour.
  • VINTAGE (a data-vintage decision, not a mechanic). 2018 data gives range 11.1, pushback 1.0, crown 40%, dmg 240@L9. Live values are range 10.1, pushback 0.7, crown 13%, dmg 220@L9. The data window from this family's evidence is 2017-10-06..2017-12-12: the roster includes Flying Machine (released 2017-10-06), while the Goblin damage and the Log crown % predate the 2017-12-12 changes. That is earlier than cards.json provenance's 'first half of 2018'.

Engine test ideas (each with its plant)

  • log_territory_is_troop_territory: Blue Log at tile (9,10) -> Ok; (9,20) -> Err(OutOfTerritory); on own princess footprint (3.5,6.5) -> Ok (no Occupied); GoblinBarrel at (9,20) -> Ok. The Python mask (action.py cell_grid) and mock_engine._check must give the same verdicts. PLANT log_territory_anywhere (map Log to Territory::Anywhere) -> (9,20) accepted -> red.
  • log_river_allowed_only_in_fallen_lane: Red left princess destroyed -> Blue Log on a left-lane river half-cell (3.0,16.0) Ok, right-lane river (14.0,16.0) Err(Water); with no tower down both are Err. PLANT log_river_never (keep the troop water check) -> the fallen-lane river cell is rejected -> red.
  • log_ground_only: Red Minion and Red Knight both at (9,12), Blue Log at (9,10), level 9: Knight loses exactly 240, Minion HP unchanged and not displaced. PLANT rolling_hits_air -> Minion damaged -> red.
  • log_pierces_and_hits_once: three Red Skeletons at (9,11),(9,13),(9,15) all die; a Red Giant at (9,12) (overlaps the rectangle for many ticks) loses exactly 240 in total. PLANT rolling_rehit_every_tick (clear the hit set each tick) -> Giant loses more than 240 -> red.
  • log_width_edge: under ROLLING_HIT_SHAPE=rect_vs_circle_edge a Red Knight centred at x = 9 tiles + 35100 + 9000 - 1 subtiles is hit, one at +1 subtile beyond is not; parameterised on the calibration key. PLANT rolling_centre_in_rect -> the inner Knight is not hit -> red.
  • log_range_end: a Red Knight whose circle overlaps the final swept rectangle by 1 subtile (roll start + ProjectileRange + 10800 + 9000 - 1) is hit, 2 subtiles further is not; ProjectileRange read from cards.json, never typed. PLANT roll_range_from_airborne_start (end = tap + range - MinDistance) -> the near-end Knight is missed -> red.
  • log_crown_tower_reduction: Blue Log placed at (3.5,14.5) with the pocket-free territory reaches the Red left princess tower. Tower HP drops by exactly 240*crown_pct/100 = 96 once at level 9. PLANT rolling_ignores_crown_pct -> drop 240 -> red; PLANT rolling_rehit_every_tick also reds it.
  • log_pushback_all_moves_heavy_units: Red Giant (IgnorePushback=true) and Red Knight on the log axis both end displaced by Pushback subtiles (after the knockback profile completes, no other units nearby), while a Fireball-style pushback without PushbackAll leaves the Giant in place. PLANT pushback_respects_ignore -> Giant unmoved -> red.
  • log_knockback_resets_windup: Red Knight in Windup against a Blue Knight is logged; the same tick after application attack_phase != Windup and his next damage lands no earlier than load_time_ms after the push. PLANT knockback_keeps_windup -> the hit lands on the original schedule -> red.
  • log_knockback_direction_lateral: Red Knight at 1.5 tiles lateral offset gets a displacement with |dx| > 0 away from the log axis under DIRECTION_ROLLING=radial_from_projectile_centre. PLANT knockback_travel_direction_only -> dx == 0 -> red.
  • log_mirror_symmetry (tests/mirror.rs): Blue Log at (x,y) with Red targets at mirrored positions vs Red Log at (x,32-y) with Blue targets; HP and positions mirror every tick, including simultaneous crossing logs. PLANT rolling_forward_plus_y_for_both -> the Red log rolls into its own king side -> red.
  • log_timing_reads_calibration: first damage tick on a victim at the tap equals the airborne ticks plus the roll ticks computed from calibration time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK (or the proposed projectile key); run at k=15 and k=18 and expect the tick index to move. PLANT inline_projectile_speed_15 -> the k=18 run keeps the k=15 tick -> red.
  • log_hits_deploying_units: Red Skeleton Army deployed on the log path the tick the roll passes; skeletons with deploy_ms > 0 die. PLANT rolling_skips_deploying -> they survive -> red.
  • log_no_friendly_fire: Blue Knight in the Blue Log's path keeps full HP and position. PLANT rolling_hits_friends -> red.
  • log_data_trap_guard: assert the Log never produces a tap-centred circular splash of radius cards.json area_damage_radius_milli; a Red Skeleton 1.9 tiles BEHIND the tap is untouched. PLANT splash_log_with_area_damage_radius -> it dies -> red.

docs.title: GoblinBarrel
docs.text:
Data chain. RAW: spells_other.GoblinBarrel.{ManaCost=3, Rarity=Epic, Projectile=GoblinBarrelSpell, OnlyEnemies=true, no SpellAsDeploy, no CanDeployOnEnemySide} -> projectiles.GoblinBarrelSpell.{Speed=400, Gravity=40, Radius=1500, AoeToGround=true, OnlyEnemies=true, Homing=(blank), no Damage, SpawnCharacter=Goblin, SpawnCharacterCount=3, SpawnCharacterDeployTime=1200, SpawnCharacterLevelIndex=5, SpawnConstPriority=TRUE} -> characters.Goblin.{Rarity=Common, Hitpoints=80, Damage=50, HitSpeed=1100, LoadTime=900, Speed=120, Range=500, SightRange=5500, CollisionRadius=500, Mass=2, DeployTime=1000 (overridden), DeployDelay=400, AttacksGround=true}; rarities.Epic.RelativeLevel=5 (== SpawnCharacterLevelIndex), rarities.Common multipliers; arena.json king_blocks[team].center = (9,3) Blue / (9,29) Red (launch origin); arena.json water bits (placement). DERIVED: cards.json cards[name=GoblinBarrel].projectile(=GoblinBarrelSpell).{speed=400, radius_milli=1500, spawn_character, spawn_character_count, spawn_character_deploy_time_ms=1200, spawn_character_level_index=5} == cards[name=GoblinBarrel].spell.spawn.{character, count, deploy_time_ms, level_index, source}; cards.json units[name=Goblin].{hitpoints, damage, hit_speed_ms, load_time_ms, speed, range_milli, sight_range_milli, collision_radius_milli, mass, deploy_time_ms, raw.DeployDelay}. GAP: card.rs loads only cards+towers, so units[name=Goblin] has no engine consumer yet.

Numbers

name value units tag source elixir cost 3 elixir DATA spells_other.GoblinBarrel.ManaCost (2018; live 3, fandom) barrel flight speed (raw) 400 raw Speed; 6000 subtiles/tick at k=15 (/60 @20TPS) or 7200 at k=18 (/50) DATA projectiles.GoblinBarrelSpell.Speed; AesDragon 2020 table 400 flight time, Blue king centre (9,3) to Red princess centre (3.5,25.5) 23.162 tiles: 69.49 ticks = 3.474 s (k=15) or 57.91 ticks = 2.895 s (k=18); to Red king (9,29): 3.900 s or 3.250 s ticks at TICK_MS=50 / seconds INFERENCE straight-line distance / (400*k); origin per fandom King's_Tower 'Launched spells ... seem to come from the King's Tower' Gravity 40 unknown arc parameter DATA GoblinBarrelSpell.Gravity Radius 1500 millitiles = 27000 subtiles distance; no damage attached (impact damage removed 2016-07-04 per fandom); fandom lists 'Radius 1.5' DATA GoblinBarrelSpell.Radius spawned unit count 3 Goblins DATA GoblinBarrelSpell.SpawnCharacterCount; fandom x3 spawned Goblin deploy time 1200 (2018); live 1100 ms, overriding characters.Goblin.DeployTime=1000 DATA GoblinBarrelSpell.SpawnCharacterDeployTime == fandom 'Goblin spawn time 1.2 seconds' (2016-07-04..2019-05-06); 1.1 s since 2019-05-06 spawn level index 5 (== rarities.Epic.RelativeLevel) level offset: Goblin unified level = barrel unified level INFERENCE GoblinBarrelSpell.SpawnCharacterLevelIndex; cross-card every spawner's index equals its rarity RelativeLevel (Witch 5, BattleRam 2, DarkWitch 8, huts/Tombstone 2); fandom 2016-01-11 fix 'Level 8 Goblin Barrel would be able to spawn Level 14 Goblins' (off-by-one of this offset) Goblin HP / damage at Common local level 1 80 / 50 hitpoints DATA characters.Goblin (pre-2017-12-12: live -6% damage, -1% HP on 2018-07-02) Goblin HP / damage from a barrel at engine unified L9 (Epic local 4) 169 / 106 hitpoints DATA 80x212/100, 50x212/100 truncating (Common local 9) Goblin HP / damage from a barrel at Epic local 1 (unified 6) 128 / 80 hitpoints DATA x160%; live fandom L6 125/75 after the 2017-12 and 2018-07 nerfs Goblin first hit after acquiring a target 200 (2018: HitSpeed 1100 - LoadTime 900); live 400 ms DATA characters.Goblin; fandom 'First Hit Speed 0.4 sec', 0.2 before 2022-10-26 Goblin speed / range / sight / radius / mass 120 / 500 / 5500 / 500 / 2 raw Speed / millitiles / millitiles / millitiles / mass DATA characters.Goblin Goblin DeployDelay 400 ms; semantics unsettled DATA characters.Goblin.DeployDelay

Behaviour, in order

  1. PLACEMENT [DATA plain spells_other row, no SpellAsDeploy; COMMUNITY fandom Goblin_Barrel trivia 'unable to be placed directly on the river', 'the only spell that cannot be placed directly on the river']: anywhere strictly inside the arena EXCEPT water half-cells (the troop closed-cell water rule is the default, INFERENCE). Bridges are legal (not water). Enemy buildings, crown towers and the king no-deploy block are legal: the canonical play is tower-centre and 'barrel the King' [COMMUNITY]. No Occupied check, no territory check. This is a NEW territory rule (Anywhere minus water) in arena.rs deploy_zone, and the Python mask's SPELL = all-ones grid must gain the same water exclusion for this card.

  2. DEPLOY: elixir 3 deducted, card cycles (existing). No deploy time for the barrel itself.

  3. LAUNCH [COMMUNITY fandom King's_Tower 'Launched spells ... seem to come from the King's Tower'; Goblin_Barrel strategy 'as soon as the Goblin Barrel is launched from the opposing King's Tower']: in the next Spawn phase create a non-entity projectile at the caster's King Tower centre (arena.json king_blocks[team].center; exact origin point unsettled) aimed at the tap point. It is not homing [DATA Homing blank]. It moves in a straight line at 400*k subtiles/tick, and the last step is clamped to land exactly on the tap [INFERENCE: Gravity treated as visual].

  4. IN FLIGHT [INFERENCE; COMMUNITY: every listed counter acts on the Goblins after landing; the 2017-10-11 Touchdown bug 'did not clear flying barrels' shows barrels are not battle entities]: the barrel is not an entity. It cannot be targeted, damaged, stunned, pushed or blocked. It ignores water, buildings and units. Its landing point is fixed at launch.

  5. ARRIVAL IMPACT [DATA no Damage; COMMUNITY 2016-07-04 'removed its impact damage']: no hits. If the spell pipeline builds a circular AoE from Radius, it must push zero hits; combat::resolve already ignores amount <= 0, so a barrel landing on the King Tower does not wake it.

  6. SPAWN [DATA SpawnCharacter/Count/DeployTime/LevelIndex; MEASURED timing, calibration spawner.RELEASE_TIMING]: on the arrival tick, release 3 Goblins (team = caster). They exist on that same frame, the one the barrel vanishes on, and are inert on it: created at the end of the tick, after the deploy countdown and the move pass, so their countdown starts on the next tick and they deploy for SpawnCharacterDeployTime / TICK_MS frames, one more than an ordinary deploy (measured on client 15.535.29: goblins first on 147, deploying 147..168, first step 170). The earlier arm, next_spawn_phase, queued them for the next Spawn phase. Level = the barrel's unified level (the Common table then gives HP/damage). deploy_ms = SpawnCharacterDeployTime (1200 in 2018, live 1100), NOT Goblin.DeployTime. Positions come from a formation around the landing point, which is unsettled. The engine default is state.rs formation for count 3: offsets (-0.5,+0.5), (+0.5,+0.5), (0,-0.5) tiles, y-mirrored for Red. Formation points on water fall back to passable ground (existing fallback).

  7. SPAWN ON A BUILDING [COMMUNITY fandom: placed at the centre of a Crown Tower the Goblins 'split apart on all sides of the Tower'; 'Crown Tower will first target the Goblin horizontally closest to the King's Tower']: spawn positions inside a building footprint are pushed out by the normal building-collision resolution (collide.rs), ending up around the tower.

  8. DEPLOYING GOBLINS [COMMUNITY: the Log 'will be able to defeat them instantly'; Mega Knight / Electro Wizard spawn damage and Giant Snowball timing all hit the Goblins during their deploy]: while deploy_ms > 0 they do not target, move or attack (target::decide already returns None), but they ARE valid victims of damage and knockback, and they occupy collision space.

  9. AFTER DEPLOY: ordinary Goblin behaviour: ground melee, AttacksGround only, sight 5500, range 500, speed 120, normal targeting (nearest target incl. crown towers per target.rs), full damage to towers (CrownTowerDamagePercent default 100).

Targets affected. The barrel itself: nothing. No damage, no pushback, no status, no king activation, no friendly fire; its AoeToGround/OnlyEnemies flags have nothing to act on. It cannot be targeted or intercepted in flight. The 3 spawned Goblins are ground melee units that attack enemy ground troops, buildings and crown towers at full damage (no crown reduction), and never attack air. They are ground victims: hittable (also while deploying) by ground- and air-targeting attacks and spells, and knockback-able (IgnorePushback false).

Unsettled

  • SPAWN FORMATION / ROLE OF Radius=1500. SETTLED 2026-09-26, measured on client 15.535.29: (c). The three Goblins stand at (0, +577) and (+-499, -288) from the landing, a ring of three touching units with one member forward (spells.PROJECTILE_SPAWN_FORMATION = count_ring_tight). Radius=1500 plays no part in it. The question as it stood: Candidates: (a) the engine's generic 3-unit grid (tight, about 1 tile span); (b) Goblins on a ring of radius Radius (1.5 tiles) around the landing point; (c) a count-dependent ring as in crforge (which dropped the 1.5-tile spread for a <1-tile triangle without evidence). The Barbarian Barrel lore (a barrel 1 tile to the side of the tower lets a 1.3-half-width roll miss one Goblin, but never the 1.95-half-width Log) is consistent with (a) and (b) once tower push-out is included, so it does not decide. DECIDING OBSERVATION: 60 fps recording of a barrel on open ground (e.g. the attacker's own side, far from buildings). Read the three Goblin positions on the first frame they are visible, then repeat 3 times at the same tile.
  • SpawnConstPriority=TRUE (only on GoblinBarrelSpell and buildings.SkeletonContainer, both containers that release units). Candidates: a deterministic (non-random) spawn layout; a constant entity update/push priority for the released units; or something about spawn ordering. DECIDING OBSERVATION: the repeated-placement recording above. An identical layout every time favours the deterministic-layout reading; nothing else in reach decides the priority reading.
  • DeployDelay=400 on Goblin. Does it stagger the 3 barrel Goblins (e.g. appearing 0/400/800 ms apart), as it may for multi-unit troop cards? The Log wiki says multi-unit cards other than Skeletons are 'slightly staggered', yet Skeleton ships DeployDelay 400 too, so the column is not simply the stagger. DECIDING OBSERVATION: frame of first visibility and of first movement for each Goblin after impact.
  • LAUNCH ORIGIN AND PATH LENGTH. King Tower centre vs another point of the king block, and straight-line horizontal distance vs arc length with Gravity=40. DECIDING OBSERVATION: flight times, release frame to landing frame, for two targets at different distances, e.g. the enemy princess centre (23.16 tiles from the king centre) and the bridge (14.12 tiles). Fit t = (d + offset)/v; a non-zero offset or a v that disagrees with the troop divisor decides.
  • SPEED DIVISOR (shared with the Log). King to enemy princess is 3.474 s at /60 and 2.895 s at /50, a difference of 0.58 s, trivially visible.
  • WATER RULE GRANULARITY. Does a tap whose half-cells merely touch the river bank count as 'on the river' (troop closed-cell rule) or is the test on the tap point only? DECIDING OBSERVATION: the placement indicator when dragging the barrel along the bank.
  • LEVEL INDEX SEMANTICS. 'Offset added to the barrel's rarity-local level' and 'same unified level as the barrel' give identical results for every shipped row, because each index equals its rarity's RelativeLevel. They only diverge for a hypothetical row whose index differs from its RelativeLevel. No observation needed for the thin slice; flag it if a future data set breaks the equality.
  • VINTAGE (a data-vintage decision): 2018 deploy 1.2 s and first hit 0.2 s, versus live deploy 1.1 s and first hit 0.4 s, plus Goblin damage -6% (2017-12-12) and HP -1% (2018-07-02).

Engine test ideas (each with its plant)

  • barrel_placement_anywhere_but_water: Blue barrel at (9,25) Ok, at the Red king centre (9,29) Ok, on the Red princess footprint (3.5,25.5) Ok, on water (9,16) Err(Water), on the left bridge (3.5,16) Ok. The Python mask and mock_engine._check must agree. PLANT barrel_anywhere_incl_water (keep Territory::Anywhere) -> the water tap is accepted -> red.
  • barrel_flight_ticks_from_king: deploy a Blue barrel at (3.5,25.5) at tick 0. No Blue Goblin exists before the arrival tick = ceil(dist(king centre, tap)/(400*k)), i.e. 70 at k=15 and 58 at k=18 with k read from calibration. Exactly 3 exist on the arrival tick itself. PLANT release_deferred -> Goblins a tick late -> red; PLANT barrel_origin_at_tap -> red.
  • barrel_goblin_deploy_time_override: every spawned Goblin has deploy_ms == cards.json GoblinBarrel.spell.spawn.deploy_time_ms (1200) on its first tick, and does not move or target until it reaches 0. PLANT spawn_uses_character_deploy_time (1000) -> red.
  • barrel_goblin_level_matches_card: barrel level 9 -> Goblin max HP 169, damage 106; barrel level 6 -> 128 / 80. PLANT spawn_level_local_one (Goblin at Common local 1) -> HP 80 -> red.
  • barrel_not_interceptable: a Red Musketeer placed under the flight path with no other Blue units acquires no target during the flight, and a Red Log rolled across the barrel's in-flight position does not cancel it (3 Goblins still spawn). PLANT barrel_is_entity (spawn the barrel as a targetable air entity) -> Musketeer fires -> red.
  • barrel_impact_is_harmless: barrel landing on the Red king (9,29): King HP unchanged on the arrival tick and the king_wake timer not started until a Goblin's hit resolves. PLANT barrel_impact_uses_goblin_damage (splash 50 at Radius 1500) -> king woken on arrival -> red.
  • barrel_on_tower_goblins_pushed_out: barrel on the Red princess centre. After the first collision passes no Goblin centre lies inside the tower footprint, and Goblins exist on both sides of the tower's x centre. PLANT no_building_block (existing plant name) -> Goblins inside the footprint -> red.
  • barrel_goblins_hittable_while_deploying: Red Log (level 9) timed to roll over the landing point while the Goblins have deploy_ms > 0 -> all 3 die (240 >= 169). PLANT rolling_skips_deploying (shared with the Log) -> they survive -> red.
  • barrel_near_water_never_spawns_on_water: barrel tapped on the last legal half-cell next to the river -> every Goblin position is passable ground on every tick of its deploy. PLANT formation_ignores_water -> a Goblin centre in water -> red.
  • barrel_mirror_symmetry (tests/mirror.rs): Blue barrel at (x,y) and Red barrel at (x,32-y) on the same tick give mirrored Goblin positions, HP and targets every tick. PLANT formation_not_y_mirrored_for_red -> red.

docs.title: Shared mechanics
docs.text:
• SPEED UNITS FOR PROJECTILES. Engine combat.rs:198 and state.rs apply time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK to projectile Speed; card.rs:57 already marks that UNVERIFIED. Evidence found 2026-09-13: fandom AesDragon (2020) asserts, without measuring, that projectile Speed is tiles/minute, the SAME unit as troop Speed. fandom Darknighture (2023) frame test: Musketeer projectile (1000) measured 1200 tiles/min and Giant (45) measured 54 tiles/min, so x1.2 (/50) for BOTH. crforge and legacy/ use /60 for both. The 'troops /50, projectiles /60' split traced to NO source. Implement ONE multiplier for both, and give projectiles their own proposed key that defaults to the troop value, so a Log roll-time or barrel flight-time recording can confirm or split it without a code change.
  • SPELL LAUNCH (non-SpellAsDeploy projectile spells: Goblin Barrel here, Fireball/Arrows in other families). Created in the Spawn phase after deploy at the caster's King Tower centre [COMMUNITY King's_Tower page], not homing, straight line to the tap, final step clamped, not an entity (untargetable, unblockable). On arrival it resolves its payload in Phase::Projectile into the damage buffer and push buffer and onto the deferred spawn queue. Arrival tick = ceil(distance/(Speed*k)).
  • TERRITORY BY SPELL FLAGS (a new function of card flags, replacing 'kind == Spell -> Anywhere' in state.rs::check_position). SpellAsDeploy=true and CanDeployOnEnemySide=false gives the troop rule (OwnHalfAndPocket) [DATA cross-card Log vs Tornado vs Miner; COMMUNITY 'only on own side']. CanDeployOnEnemySide=true lifts the side restriction (Tornado; not in slice). CanPlaceOnBuildings=true skips Occupied. A projectile spell whose projectile has SpawnCharacter gets Anywhere minus water [COMMUNITY Goblin Barrel river trivia]. SpellAsDeploy cards may also use river cells of a lane whose enemy princess is down [COMMUNITY 2018-04-25, Log and Barbarian Barrel]. CONSUMERS that must change in the same commit: crates/royalesim/src/arena.rs (Territory enum + deploy_zone), state.rs::check_position, py.rs DeployError codes if a new reason appears, RoyaleGym/royalegym/protocol.py Placement (ROLLING doc, and a SPELL-not-on-water variant), RoyaleGym/royalegym/action.py cell_grid (SPELL is all-ones today; ROLLING excludes all water), RoyaleGym/royalegym/mock_engine.py _check and the loader at line 365 (maps every SpellAsDeploy card to ROLLING, which is wrong for Tornado because CanDeployOnEnemySide=true). tests/test_rust_engine.py already asserts mask/engine equality of the pocket rule; extend it to the new rules.
  • ROLLING (PIERCING) PROJECTILE LAW. Straight along team-forward, speed Speed*k, total travel ProjectileRange from roll start, swept axis-aligned rectangle (half-width ProjectileRadius, half-depth ProjectileRadiusY) tested against victim circles edge-to-edge (shape key). Enemy-only per OnlyEnemies, air/ground per AoeToAir/AoeToGround, a per-projectile hit set so each entity is hit at most once, crown pct through damage_against, level scaling of the caster card. The rectangle-circle test is new integer geometry and belongs in fixed.rs. The same law serves the Bowler and Barbarian Barrel later (BowlerProjectile ProjectileRadius 1000, ProjectileRange 6000).
  • SpellAsDeploy AIRBORNE PHASE. A first projectile (LogProjectile: Speed 360, MinDistance 3000, Gravity 30, no Damage) with no hitbox whose arrival spawns SpawnProjectile at its landing point, inheriting team, card level and forward direction. Launch geometry is the open key spells.SPELL_AS_DEPLOY_LAUNCH_MODEL.
  • KNOCKBACK LAW (shared with Fireball and any Pushback source). Distance = Pushback millitiles x18 subtiles [COMMUNITY history: Log 1 tile <-> 1000]. Applied only to troops (not buildings or towers). Skipped for IgnorePushback units UNLESS the source has PushbackAll=true [DATA + COMMUNITY]. Recorded in a buffer during the phase that produced the hit and applied after Resolve to survivors as summed displacements, so the order cannot matter and tie-breaks stay mirror-invariant. Resets the victim's attack windup [COMMUNITY]. Not blocked by water the way walking is [COMMUNITY river lore]. Units mid-jump are immune. Direction (radial from the source centre is the default for both circular and rolling sources), time profile, mass dependence and water/building resolution are all calibration keys with no primary source. The engine does not load ignore_pushback today (card.rs has no field); cards.json already carries it.
  • SPAWN-ON-ARRIVAL. A projectile with SpawnCharacter enqueues SpawnCharacterCount units of that character on the deferred spawn queue at its arrival point. Level = caster's unified level (SpawnCharacterLevelIndex equals the caster rarity RelativeLevel in every shipped row). deploy_ms = SpawnCharacterDeployTime when present, else the character's DeployTime. Formation is a key. Water fallback is the existing formation rule. card.rs must load cards.json units[] (Goblin) because no card in the thin slice summons a plain Goblin; the same loader serves death spawns later.
  • VALID SPELL VICTIMS. Deploying units are hittable and pushable (combat::splash already does not skip deploy_ms > 0; keep that for rolling hits). Untargetable states exclude victims: hidden Tesla (live: immune to all damage except Earthquake/Freeze), units mid-jump, and the Skeleton Barrel's 0.5 s release animation (not in slice). Friendly units never, for OnlyEnemies=true sources.
  • CROWN TOWER DAMAGE PERCENT = 100 + raw column, applied to King and Princess towers with truncating integer division (combat::damage_against). The Log's -60 <-> the wiki's 40% before 2017-12-12 is independent corroboration of the delta-from-100 hypothesis in cards.json conventions.
  • DATA VINTAGE FINDING (not a mechanic). This family's numbers (Log crown 40%, roll 11.1, Goblin damage 50, barrel deploy 1.2 s) plus the roster (Flying Machine released 2017-10-06, no Royal Ghost) date csv_logic to about 2017-10-06..2017-12-12, earlier than cards.json provenance 'first half of 2018'. Live-2026 deltas for this family (fandom): Log range 10.1, pushback 0.7, crown 13%, damage 220@L9; barrel Goblin deploy 1.1 s, first hit 0.4 s. Whether to overlay them is a project decision: the target is the live 2026 game, and card stats are evidence, not spec.

docs.title: Calibration keys proposed
docs.text:
• time.PROJECTILE_SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK -- status: hypothesis, tied to time.SPEED_TO_SUBTILES_PER_TICK (default equal). Provenance: card.rs:57 UNVERIFIED; AesDragon asserts same unit; Darknighture frame test shows x1.2 for both; no source for a split. Promotion: live Log roll duration, first contact to despawn (3.03 s at /60, 2.525 s at /50), and Goblin Barrel flight time king centre to enemy princess centre (3.474 s vs 2.895 s). Split from the troop key only if a projectile measurement disagrees with the troop measurement beyond frame error.
  • spells.SPELL_LAUNCH_ORIGIN -- candidates king_tower_centre (default) | king_block_front_edge. Status guess, COMMUNITY qualitative ('seem to come from the King's Tower'). Promotion: fit the offset in t = (d + offset)/v from barrel flight times to two targets at different distances.
  • spells.PROJECTILE_PATH_LENGTH -- candidates straight_line_horizontal (default, Gravity visual) | arc_length_with_gravity. Status guess. Promotion: the same two-distance flight-time fit; arc length makes the time non-linear in distance.
  • spells.SPELL_AS_DEPLOY_LAUNCH_MODEL -- candidates airborne_from_behind_lands_on_tap (default) | airborne_from_tap_forward_range_from_tap | instant_roll_at_tap. Status guess. Promotion: Log recording with a Skeleton on the tap tile and one 1.5 tiles ahead; which is hit, and frames from release to first damage (0.5 s / 0.417 s / ~0).
  • spells.ROLLING_MIN_DISTANCE_SEMANTICS -- candidates ignored_when_range_set (default) | no_hit_zone_from_roll_start | minimum_travel. Status guess. Promotion: the same recording; a Skeleton 1 tile ahead of the tap survives only under no_hit_zone.
  • spells.ROLLING_HIT_SHAPE -- candidates rect_vs_circle_edge (default, matches combat::splash edge convention) | rect_contains_centre. Status guess; 2023-03-27 'improved collision detection' changed it unspecifiedly. Promotion: Skeletons at 2.2 tiles lateral offset from the log axis.
  • knockback.DIRECTION_ROLLING -- candidates radial_from_projectile_centre (default; three fandom lateral-push strategy lines) | travel_direction (crforge) | from_centre_segment. Status guess. Promotion: displacement vector of a Knight struck 1.5 tiles off-axis.
  • knockback.PROFILE -- candidates instant | linear_over_ms (with knockback.DURATION_MS). Status guess, no column or global exists. Promotion: count frames of the slide on a logged Skeleton.
  • knockback.MASS_SCALING -- candidates none (default: Pushback is a distance) | mass_weighted. Status guess; 'a field existing is not a formula'. Promotion: Skeleton (mass 1) and Giant (mass 18) logged side by side.
  • knockback.WATER_AND_BUILDING_RESOLUTION -- candidates allow_overlap_then_nearest_passable (default; river-crossing lore) | clamp_at_obstacle. Status guess. Promotion: Log a Knight on the bridge exit and one on a bank.
  • knockback.ATTACK_RESET -- candidates reset_windup_keep_target (default) | reset_windup_and_clear_target. The reset itself is COMMUNITY-settled; only target retention is open. Promotion: frames from push to next hit of a Knight attacking a tower.
  • spawn.PROJECTILE_SPAWN_FORMATION -- candidates engine_grid (default, state.rs formation) | ring_at_projectile_radius (GoblinBarrelSpell.Radius 1500) | count_ring_tight. Status guess. Promotion: first-visible-frame Goblin positions from a barrel on open ground, repeated 3x.
  • spawn.SPAWNED_UNITS_STAGGER_BY_DEPLOY_DELAY -- candidates false (default) | true (characters.DeployDelay, Goblin 400 ms). Status guess. Promotion: per-Goblin first-visible and first-move frames after impact.
  • arena.SPELL_AS_DEPLOY_RIVER_WHEN_LANE_TOWER_DOWN -- candidates lane_half_of_river (default) | whole_river | none. Status: COMMUNITY that some river placement is allowed (2018-04-25); cell set guess. Promotion: drag the Log over river cells in both lanes after one princess falls. Must be the same key for the Rust deploy_zone and the Python mask (as POCKET_DEPTH_HALF_ROWS is).
  • arena.SPELL_AS_DEPLOY_ON_NO_DEPLOY_CELLS -- candidates blocked (default, troop rule) | allowed (CanPlaceOnBuildings extends to the king block). Status guess. Promotion: placement indicator over own King Tower and the river-corner tiles (0,14)/(17,14).
  • arena.SPAWNING_SPELL_WATER_RULE -- candidates closed_cell_touch (default, troop rule) | point_only. Status guess; the rule that the barrel cannot land on water is COMMUNITY-settled. Promotion: placement indicator dragging the barrel along the river bank.

docs.title: README media
docs.text:
Every file the README embeds, and how to make it again.

Everything here is generated. The generator is RoyaleGym/docs/media/make_media.py, which lives in RoyaleGym because it writes into all four repos and the four are cloned side by side. From the folder that holds the repos, in Windows PowerShell:

.venv\Scripts\python RoyaleGym\docs\media\make_media.py --list
.venv\Scripts\python RoyaleGym\docs\media\make_media.py battle-page determinism

It needs the engine built, royalegym and royaleviser installed, and Pillow. The videos also need RoyaleViser's media extra, which supplies ffmpeg; without it the videos are skipped and the stills are still written. Re-running it gives the same bytes: the battle is played on a fixed seed with a named deck, and the viewer's capture freezes the two numbers on screen that move with the wall clock.

Each video is a .gif and an .mp4 of the same thing. The README points at the gif, because GitHub plays a gif inside an <img> tag and will not play an mp4 there. The mp4 is the better copy for anyone who opens the file directly.

File How it is made What it shows battle-page.gif / .mp4 make_media.py battle-page The busiest stretch of an engine battle in RoyaleViser, found by sweeping the trace for the tick with the most units alive. One frame per engine tick. cards-and-spells.gif / .mp4 make_media.py cards-and-spells A spell landing on a crowd late in the same battle, found the same way: the tick with a spell in the air and the most units on the board. deploy-legality.png make_media.py deploy-legality The arena coloured by what check_deploy answers for one card, before and after an enemy princess tower falls. determinism.png make_media.py determinism One seed run more than once, with the per-tick state hashes side by side. throughput.png make_media.py throughput A real transcript of tools/throughput.py, and what the rate means in whole battles an hour. snapshots.png make_media.py snapshots One saved position loaded into several engines and stepped on differently. ledger.png make_media.py ledger The spread of statuses across data/calibration.json: every entry counted, in four bands from measured to guess. engine-battle-viewer.png a RoyaleViser screenshot final, not regenerated here family.svg hand-drawn the Royale repos and how they depend on each other; final

docs.title: Still placeholders, and why
docs.text:
A placeholder is a generated SVG whose alt text begins "Image placeholder:" or "Video placeholder:" and says what the real picture must show. Replace the file, keep the name.

File What it must show Why it is not made here measured-routes.svg one deploy, two routes on one board: the recorded route and the engine's, node for node, plus the 743 of 744 score Nobody has made it yet. It CAN be made: crates/royalesim/tests/fixtures/oracle2026/client16402_first_paths.json carries 747 cases, each with the recorded route (oracle_cells_goal_first) and the request the engine needs to plan the same one, so both routes come from the repo. contact-law.svg a real battle and the engine side by side over 20 ticks, a crowd dropped onto a defender spreading apart Nobody has made it yet. crates/royalesim/tests/fixtures/replay/sample.json carries 1,178 ticks of per-tick positions for 16 entities, so the picture's INPUT is committed; whether that particular battle contains a scene that shows the law is not checked. It holds Prince, Dark Prince, Skeletons, Battle Ram, Giant and Musketeer.

Those two tiles carry the project's strongest claims, so they are worth making properly rather than approximating. Both are drawn from committed fixtures plus a running engine, which is the rule for every public picture here: it comes from the engine or from data already in the repo, and a script anyone with a clone can run.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to RoyaleViser. Versions follow Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• The window library is pygame-ce instead of pygame. It is used the same way (import pygame) and installs on Python 3.14, which pygame does not. Uninstall pygame first if you have it: the two share the pygame folder.
  • CI also installs and tests the viewer on Python 3.14.
  • The guide tells a pip install user to skip Setup, which is only for working on the viewer.

The first tagged version: recordings, saved battles and a running engine in one window, with the compare ghost, the inspector, pictures and clips.

  • A royaleviser command. On its own it waits for a training run on 127.0.0.1:9870 and shows it live. Given a folder, it opens the newest saved battle in it.
  • royaleviser --version and royaleviser.__version__.
  • Saved battles show the special forms: hero cards are crowned, and evolved cards count their plays. A battle saved with RoyaleGym 2f710e8 or later also shows the ability buttons.
  • A missing file, an empty folder or a missing RoyaleGym is reported in one line, not a traceback.
  • Busy frames send on macOS (its default socket buffer refused a datagram over 9 KB).
  • CI on Windows, Ubuntu and macOS.
  • Opening a saved battle whose step log holds an ability press no longer crashes.
  • Two cards in one deck can no longer show the same small-tile code.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thanks for helping. Bug reports, fixes and new drawing ideas are all welcome.

docs.title: Set up
docs.text:
Follow the guide's Setup, then install the test tools:

pip install -e ".[dev,media]"

docs.title: Before you open a pull request
docs.text:
Run the same two checks CI runs, from the RoyaleViser folder:

python -m pytest -q
python -m ruff check royaleviser tests

Some tests skip on your machine and say why in their skip line, for example when no engine is built. A skip is not a pass, and CI runs the rest.

docs.title: RoyaleViser guide
docs.text:
Watch a Clash Royale battle play out, one step at a time, in a window on your own machine.

It opens three kinds of thing: a recording of a real match, a battle saved to a file by the engine, or a bot that is training right now in another program.

Try it  ·  What it does  ·  Save a picture  ·  The rest of the stack  ·  Status  ·  Community

You can try this one without building the engine: clone it, install one package, run one command. You do not need any game files either. Jump to Try it.

Every command on this page is for Windows PowerShell, one per line. Paste them one at a time rather than as a block. PowerShell cannot chain commands with &&, and a pasted # comment is not a comment in cmd. On macOS and Linux the interpreter is .venv/bin/python, paths use forward slashes, cp replaces Copy-Item, and export X=Y sets a variable. Where a line differs in any other way, its macOS and Linux form is given beside it.

That is a battle the engine played against itself, saved to a file and reopened here. On the left you get both players' hands, their elixir to a thousandth, the next card and a running log of what happened. On the right you get every single thing the file knows about the Blue Valkyrie that was clicked. The bar underneath scrubs through the replay.

The point of the viewer is simple. You can see what your bot did instead of guessing it from numbers. And you can lay two sources of one battle over each other and see the ticks where they disagree.

It draws one picture per tick. A tick is the game's own 50 ms step, so 20 of them go by every second.

It always runs as its own separate program. Your training run never waits for it. When nobody is watching, it costs your training run almost nothing.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Installed with pip install "royalegym[all]"? You already have royaleviser. Skip Setup: it is only for working on the viewer itself.

The install gives you a royaleviser command. It opens three ways:

  • royaleviser on its own waits for a training run on 127.0.0.1:9870 and shows it live.
  • royaleviser FILE opens a saved battle (.msgpack, .json, .jsonl or .jsonl.gz).
  • royaleviser FOLDER opens the newest saved battle anywhere in that folder.

python -m royaleviser is the same program. The examples below use it, so they also work straight from a clone.

The rest of this section uses files that only a clone of this repo has. Two recordings of the same scripted battle, one from each player's point of view, are committed with the tests. They are about 20 KB each, so they came down with your clone.

You need the shared virtual environment from Setup and this one package installed. Nothing else. No engine build, no game files, no recordings of your own. Then move into the RoyaleViser folder with cd RoyaleViser and run this one command:

..\.venv\Scripts\python -m royaleviser tests\fixtures\frames-synthetic-A.jsonl.gz --compare tests\fixtures\frames-synthetic-B.jsonl.gz --speed 4 --seconds 8

A window opens and plays the battle at 4x speed. On a computer with no screen, such as a Linux server, no window appears and nothing tells you so. The end of this section shows how to run it there.

The second recording is drawn on top of the first as hollow ghosts. Nothing differs between these two recordings, so the ghosts sit exactly on the units and never step off. The compare panel finishes at 395 ticks compared, 0 differ, under a GAME OVER Blue wins banner.

That battle is a script, not something the engine played. One frame of the recording stands for six ticks of the script, so the units move at six times their scripted speed. It is an honest look at the window and a poor look at how the engine plays.

After eight seconds the program closes itself and prints how many pictures it drew and how long they took. This is one run on the machine this page was written on (2026-09-21):

royaleviser: 290 draws, mean 4.08 ms, max 370.22 ms

That is 290 pictures at 4.08 ms each on average. A replay needs 20 a second, so that machine had a lot of room to spare. The 370 ms is the very first draw, which builds the board and loads the fonts.

Your numbers will differ. They depend on your machine and on what else it is running. On 2026-09-28, on a machine with a training run busy on every core, five runs of this command with no window drew between 15 and 143 pictures.

Drop --seconds and the window stays open until you close it.

The same command opens the other kinds of source. One of them at a time, not all three.

The three lines below, and the other bare python lines on this page, assume the venv is active: ..\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 in PowerShell, source ../.venv/bin/activate on macOS and Linux, from the RoyaleViser folder. Without it, python is your system Python and the error names a missing package such as pygame or msgspec. If PowerShell refuses to run Activate.ps1, write the venv's python by path instead: ..\.venv\Scripts\python.

A recording of a real battle. Real recordings come from RoyaleLive, which is private, so your clone has none. The two scripted recordings in tests/fixtures open this way, and so does a recording of your own in the format docs/internals.md describes. frames-my-match.jsonl.gz stands for your file's name:

python -m royaleviser frames-my-match.jsonl.gz

A trace saved from the engine, opened at tick 900. This one needs RoyaleGym, from the rest of Setup. battle.msgpack is the file the program in Saving a battle to a file writes, in the folder you ran that program from. Run this from that folder, or give the file's path:

python -m royaleviser battle.msgpack --start-tick 900

An environment that is running right now, in another process:

python -m royaleviser --stream 127.0.0.1:9870

Keys in the window: space plays and pauses. The arrow keys step one frame. A click pins a unit, or seeks the timeline if you click the bar. c turns the compare ghost on and off. s saves a PNG. h lists every key there is.

No screen? Set two variables first. SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy runs the viewer with no window, on purpose. SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy stops the sound errors (ALSA, on Linux) that a machine with no sound device prints. The viewer makes no sound anyway. Then add --shot to save the last picture as a PNG. In PowerShell:

$env:SDL_VIDEODRIVER = "dummy"
$env:SDL_AUDIODRIVER = "dummy"
..\.venv\Scripts\python -m royaleviser tests\fixtures\frames-synthetic-A.jsonl.gz --compare tests\fixtures\frames-synthetic-B.jsonl.gz --speed 4 --seconds 8 --shot shot.png

On Linux the first two lines are export SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy and export SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy. The command prints royaleviser: saved shot.png and the draw times, and shot.png shows GAME OVER Blue wins and 395 ticks compared, 0 differ. The two variables stay set until you close that shell.

The seat, the window size, --seconds, --shot and the rest of the command line are in docs/internals.md.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Replay a recorded matchPlay, pause, step one frame, seek by clicking the bar. The clip is the scripted battle that ships with the tests, so its motion is scripted rather than played by the engine. Open an engine traceA battle saved from the engine with one frame per tick. Open it at any tick you like. Watch a training run liveAttach to a training run in another program. With nobody watching it costs that run 193 ns a step (2026-09-21). Compare two recordings of one battleTwo recordings of one battle should agree, and the viewer says so tick by tick. Here both players recorded the scripted battle that ships with the tests: 395 ticks compared, 0 differ. See where they disagreeThe second source is drawn as hollow ghosts on the first. On a tick where they differ, the ghost steps off the unit. The two recordings in this clip are identical, so nothing steps off here. Inspect any unitClick a unit to list every field the source carries, raw and unrounded, except an effect's time left, which shows in tenths of a second. Follow the event logPlays, spawns, deaths and tunnel trips (Miner, Goblin Drill), each with its tick and tile, newest last. Paths and target linesRecorded units carry the route they walk and the thing they attack. Two keys draw both on the board. Here a Baby Dragon is walking its route while the Cannon aims at it. Render with no displaySave the window as a PNG with no screen. A scripted battle ships with the tests, so nothing else is needed.

The cards. Each card in a hand is a tile. Its colour and the mark in its corner say whether it is a troop, a building or a spell. The big letters are its name, and the purple drop is its cost. A card fills in from the bottom as elixir comes in, so you can see how close it is to being played, and its white border appears once it can be played. The next card is the small tile by the elixir bar. Two cards can have the same big letters, like Witch and Wizard. When both are in the deck, the small tile shows other letters for each: Wt and Wz.

Evolutions and heroes. An evolved card gets a dot for each time it was played since its last evolution, and a pink frame with an EVO tag when its next play is the evolution. A hero card wears a gold crown, and its ability button sits next to the elixir bar: gold when it can be used, crossed out once it has been, and grey with the seconds left while it waits. A champion's button works the same way. On the board, an evolved unit gets a pink ring and a hero a gold one. A unit travelling under ground (Miner, Goblin Drill) is a patch of dirt, and an invisible one is faded. The board marks show in every source. The hand marks show when you watch a running battle that has evolutions or heroes, and in a saved trace too: it knows the deck's heroes, and it counts each evolved card's plays again from the battle. A trace saved with RoyaleGym 2f710e8 or later keeps the engine's own rows, ability buttons included; an older one shows no buttons.

Units on one spot. Two units of one team can stand on almost the same spot. Then you only see the one on top, so its name gets a count, like RamRider x2. A Ram Rider's rider sits on its ram. A battle from the engine says so, and there the rider is drawn as a small seat with a white rim on top of its ram. A recording of a real match does not say, so there it shows x2.

docs.title: Save a picture or a clip
docs.text:
You can take a picture of any of this for your own write-up. capture writes what the window would show straight to a file, with no window, no display and no clock. It is what made the images on this page. This example opens the recording that came with your clone, so it runs from the repo folder with nothing else set up. Swap in your own file or an engine trace, which Saving a battle to a file makes.

from royaleviser.capture import capture
from royaleviser.sources import open_source

capture(open_source("tests/fixtures/frames-synthetic-A.jsonl.gz"), "shot.png",
        ticks=(160, 161, 1), scale=24, crop="left")

The whole signature:

capture(source, out, *, ticks=None, scale=24, view=None, crop="full", fps=20,
        compare=None, theme=DEFAULT, live_timing=False) -> list[Path]
  • The suffix picks the format. .png writes one file per frame, numbered name-0000.png when the range holds more than one. .mp4 and .gif encode the range at fps.
  • ticks is (start, stop, step) in battle ticks, the clock the window shows, not frame indices. Without it the whole source is captured.
  • crop is full, board, left, or a rectangle. left drops the inspector column.
  • compare ghosts a second source at the same tick. view carries the seat, the overlays and hover_uid, which pins a unit in the inspector.
  • The same source and the same arguments give you the same bytes, always. Two numbers move with the wall clock: the draw time and the frame rate. Both are zero in every capture, and the LIVE pill is never drawn, because a capture replays a file. live_timing=True adds the source's own status line, which is built from the file, so it is reproducible too.
  • PNG needs nothing extra. mp4 and gif are encoded by ffmpeg, which comes with the optional media extra.

For a sense of size: the whole scripted battle cropped to left at scale 16, every 8th tick (ticks=(0, 395, 8)), is a 0.27 MB gif (2026-09-28).

docs.title: With the rest of the stack
docs.text:
Repo What it is To the viewer RoyaleSim the battle engine, written in Rust. It uses whole numbers only, and the same battle always plays out the same way. Its movement is measured against recordings of real battles every trace and every stream starts here RoyaleGym the layer your bot plugs into: what it sees, what it can do, what it gets rewarded for. Gymnasium, PettingZoo and self-play flavours the only sibling this package imports. It gives the viewer the trace format (royalegym.replay), the engine-side sender (royalegym.viser.ViserPublisher, a publisher in the code) and the shape of the arena RoyaleLearn the training side: bots playing themselves, PPO (a common training algorithm), a ladder of frozen past opponents, saved checkpoints a training run streams to the viewer like any other environment RoyaleViser (this repo) the viewer: recordings, engine traces and running environments, in its own window the window RoyaleImitate an optional add-on to RoyaleLearn: config sections that start a bot from saved weights and keep it near a reference policy while it learns nothing RoyaleLive private. It records real battles it writes the recordings the viewer replays and compares

If you already know RLGym, RocketSim and rlviser, this is the same split. An environment API on top of an engine, a learner on top of that, and the viewer off in its own process.

What goes in. Three things.

  • A recording of a real battle: frames-*.jsonl or .jsonl.gz, one line of JSON per frame, 20 frames a second.
  • A trace saved from the engine: .msgpack or .json, written by royalegym.replay.ReplayRecorder.
  • A stream from a program running right now: UDP datagrams from a ViserPublisher, one per environment step.

What comes out. PNG stills and mp4 or gif clips, the compare totals, and one frame object (royaleviser.model.Frame) that any other front end can draw from.

The three formats, the rules every frame has to follow and the stream protocol are in docs/internals.md.

docs.title: Saving a battle to a file
docs.text:
Save a battle from the engine and you can reopen it here later, at any tick. RoyaleGym's ReplayRecorder writes the file. Pass it frame_every_tick=True and it keeps every single engine tick instead of one frame per environment step:

import numpy as np
from royalegym import (ClashParallelEnv, RandomLegalOpponent, ReplayRecorder,
                       RustEngine, StepLimitCondition, save_trace)

rec = ReplayRecorder(frame_every_tick=True)
env = ClashParallelEnv(RustEngine(),          # RustEngine: the RoyaleSim engine, from Python
                       recorder=rec, truncation_cond=StepLimitCondition(200))
obs, _ = env.reset(seed=2026)
rng, opp = np.random.default_rng(0), RandomLegalOpponent(noop_prob=0.3)
while env.agents:
    obs, *_ = env.step({a: opp.act(obs[a], obs[a]["action_mask"], rng) for a in env.agents})
save_trace(rec.trace, "battle.msgpack")      # 200 steps -> 2001 frames, one per tick

200 steps of the environment turn into 2001 frames, one per tick.

docs.title: Watching a run that is happening now
docs.text:
A running environment sends frames out instead of writing a file. Set one environment variable and change no code, or hand it a sender yourself. Then attach from another program.

Nothing is sent until a viewer says hello. Sending stops three seconds after the last viewer goes away. So you can leave this switched on in a training run you are not watching.

Three things happen, in three different places. First, in the shell where the training run will start and before it starts, name the address the frames go to. In PowerShell:

$env:ROYALEVISER = "127.0.0.1:9870"

In cmd it is set ROYALEVISER=127.0.0.1:9870. On macOS and Linux it is export ROYALEVISER=127.0.0.1:9870. A set line typed into PowerShell or bash sets nothing, and the viewer then waits for frames that never come.

The vectorised environment reads that when you build it. It binds one publisher and watches game 0. None of your own code changes. Frames only go out while the environment steps, so something has to step it: your training loop does. This stand-in plays random legal moves in eight games on the engine:

import numpy as np
from royalegym import ClashParallelEnv, ClashSelfPlayVecEnv, RustEngine

env = ClashSelfPlayVecEnv(8, lambda: ClashParallelEnv(RustEngine()))
env.reset(seed=0)
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
for _ in range(2000):
    masks = env.action_masks()
    env.step([rng.choice(np.flatnonzero(m)) for m in masks])

It ran for 87 seconds on a busy machine on 2026-09-28, which is time enough to attach the viewer. Leave out the lambda and the games run on MockEngine, the pure-Python stand-in, with a warning that no engine was chosen.

Then, in another process, attach the viewer to that same address:

python -m royaleviser --stream 127.0.0.1:9870

A viewer shows one battle at a time. When you run eight games at once, something has to pick which one. So the vectorised environment is the thing that reads ROYALEVISER: it opens the sender once and hands it to game 0. Eight games all reaching for the viewer's one UDP port is an error, not eight streams.

9870 is a default, not the address. One run holds that port while it streams, so a second run on the same machine needs its own: ROYALEVISER=127.0.0.1:9872, and a viewer pointed at the same number. A second run started on a port that is taken stops with an OSError as soon as it builds the environment. The message says the port is already in use, almost always by another run of yours, and tells you to pick another one.

A single environment reads no environment variable of its own. You hand it a sender directly. ViserPublisher comes from royalegym.viser, and on its own it sends to 127.0.0.1:9870:

from royalegym import ClashParallelEnv, RustEngine
from royalegym.viser import ViserPublisher

env = ClashParallelEnv(RustEngine(), viser=ViserPublisher())

While a viewer is attached, one msgpack datagram goes out per engine tick. Measured on 2026-09-20 on MockEngine, the pure-Python stand-in, not the Rust engine above: 2.6 KB for 18 units (12 troops and the 6 towers, which are units of their own kind, not a list beside them), and 11 KB for 60. Since 2026-09-24 each unit also carries its target and the effects on it, and each frame carries the shots in flight, so a datagram is bigger now. It has not been measured again.

That is a real stream, not the scripted battle. Another process is stepping four self-play battles on the engine and publishing game 0, and everything in the window arrived over the socket.

Two things in it are worth reading, and both are properties rather than measurements. The learner panel is empty because nothing was training when the shot was taken. And the status line admits dropped frames: the viewer drops them rather than slowing the environment down, which is the trade it is built to make, and it tells you when it has. On the occasion this shot was taken, with four other jobs running, that was 86 frames of 116.

docs.title: Showing your training numbers next to the battle
docs.text:
The learner can report too, on its own port, and the panel in the dashboard fills in:

import time

from royaleviser.model import Learning
from royaleviser.sources import LearningPublisher

learner = LearningPublisher()                     # 127.0.0.1:9871, the stream's port plus one
for it in range(60):
    time.sleep(1)                                 # your rollout and optimise step go here
    learner.publish(Learning(run="ppo-0007", iteration=it, policy_loss=0.0241, elo=1183))

Run it, then attach a viewer from another window with --stream 127.0.0.1:9870. The panel fills within a second or two, and its iteration counts up once a second.

That is the same window on a live battle. The panel under the event log is the learner's, and every number in it arrived over the network. The numbers in this picture come from a script, not from a real learner.

It is sent separately from the battle frames and on its own clock, once per training iteration rather than once per step. So it keeps updating while the learner is busy and nothing on the board is moving. A viewer that attaches in the middle of a run is sent the last status right away, instead of waiting for the next iteration.

The heading shows how long ago the last status arrived. On a real run the board stands still while the learner trains, and that age is how you tell a slow run from a dead one.

One message is the whole status. That is the contract, not a matter of taste: the viewer replaces what it is holding rather than merging the new message into the old one, so the panel never shows a mixture the learner never sent at one moment.

A field your learner does not send shows a dash. The panel never puts a zero there. Nobody reported that number, so it does not pretend one.

Anything the twenty fixed rows cannot hold goes in Learning.extra, which is {name: number or string}, drawn underneath in the order you sent it.

If you would rather your learner did not import this package, it can send the same small msgpack datagram itself. The format and the six constants it has to match are in docs/internals.md.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Installed with pip install "royalegym[all]"? You already have royaleviser. Skip this section: the clones, the virtual environment and Rust below are only for working on the viewer itself.

The whole stack shares one setup. The repos sit side by side in one folder, with one virtual environment at its root. You do not need all of it to use the viewer, so it comes in two parts.

The short way, for the viewer on its own. No Rust, no engine build, no game files. You need Python 3.12 or newer and git. Run these from wherever you keep your projects, one line at a time:

mkdir Royale
cd Royale
git clone https://github.com/RoyaleGym/RoyaleViser.git
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python --version
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e RoyaleViser

The venv line asks for Python 3.12 by name. On macOS and Linux it is python3.12 -m venv .venv. If python --version already prints 3.12 or newer, python -m venv .venv works too. The version line must print 3.12 or newer before you go on. With an older Python, pip refuses the install line.

The last line downloads pygame-ce, msgspec and numpy, which is a few tens of MB. You now have the two recordings that ship with the tests, and the board is drawn from a copy of the arena built into this package. That is enough for Try it, for streams, and for saving a PNG.

The rest of the stack, if you want to open an engine trace or record one yourself. Do the short way first, because the rest builds on the folder, the environment and the clone it made. The engine is Rust, so this part also needs a Rust toolchain from rustup.rs. Add the other three clones and the build tools, from the Royale folder:

git clone https://github.com/RoyaleGym/RoyaleSim.git
git clone https://github.com/RoyaleGym/RoyaleGym.git
git clone https://github.com/RoyaleGym/RoyaleLearn.git
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install maturin pytest hypothesis ruff numpy msgspec

Next, generate the card and arena data the engine reads, in RoyaleSim/data/derived/. The engine cannot start without it. A clone carries only cards-15.535.json in data/derived/; these lines generate the rest. The copy line is the important one: cards-15.535.json is the table the engine loads. The extract_cards.py --vintage 2018 line still runs, building the older table beside it for the cross-engine comparisons that use it. On macOS and Linux the copy is cp data/derived/cards-15.535.json data/derived/cards.json.

cd RoyaleSim
..\.venv\Scripts\python tools\extract_arena.py
..\.venv\Scripts\python tools\extract_cards.py --vintage 2018
Copy-Item data\derived\cards-15.535.json data\derived\cards.json
..\.venv\Scripts\python tools\extract_globals.py

Then build the engine into the environment, from that same RoyaleSim folder. Give it a few minutes and some free memory. It can go quiet for a minute or more on the engine itself; let it finish:

..\.venv\Scripts\maturin develop --release
cd ..

Then install the Python packages, back in the Royale folder:

.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e RoyaleGym
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e RoyaleViser
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e RoyaleLearn

One more line, only if you want to train. It is a big download:

.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e "RoyaleLearn[torch]"

Here is what each piece of the viewer needs.

  • Recordings, streams and the scripted battle need only the virtual environment and pip install -e RoyaleViser. That pulls in pygame-ce, msgspec and numpy. Without RoyaleGym the board is drawn from a copy of the arena built into this package.
  • Opening a trace needs RoyaleGym as well. RoyaleGym then reads the arena out of the RoyaleSim checkout (data/derived/, which the extract_* lines above generate), not out of the engine build.
  • Recording a trace yourself needs the engine build too, so you need the whole recipe.
  • mp4 and gif out of capture need the media extra, which brings ffmpeg with it. A PNG needs nothing beyond this package.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The test badge is a clone's run at 500ae04, measured with ROYALELIVE_REPORTS pointed at an empty folder. On a machine that has the recordings the same pytest run is 372 passed, 1 skipped.

As of 2026-09-22, this works end to end:

  • Replaying a recording, and comparing two recordings of one battle. The pair that ships with the tests gives 395 ticks compared, 0 differ.
  • Drawing a building at the size the source says it stands on. When a source does not carry that size, the viewer marks what it drew rather than guessing quietly: red corner ticks and a count of how many sizes on screen are guesses. Since 2026-09-22 frames and traces carry the size, so a Cannon is the 3 by 3 building it is in the game, and the marking is there for older files and for sources that do not carry one.
  • A building is drawn as two shapes, because it has two different sizes and they are easy to confuse. The box is the ground it stands on. A new building only goes where its whole box fits, so one tapped too close to another is moved to a spot nearby where it does. The circle inside is its collision radius, which is what other units bump into. On the engine a Cannon stands on 3 tiles with a radius of 0.6 of a tile, a princess tower 3 and 1.0, and a king tower 4 and 1.4 (2026-09-22). A source that carries no radius gets no circle rather than a guessed one.
  • Traces from the engine. A 2001-frame self-play trace draws, and every frame of it passes the viewer's own consistency check.
  • Streaming from a running environment. A stream carries one frame per engine tick. On 2026-09-24 a 3,728-tick battle, slowed to about 20 seconds so a person could watch it, sent 3,528 frames, none of them dropped for being too big to send. The viewer's own count of frames lost on the way was not read. The viewer was open before the battle started. The missing first second is the time the run took to hear the viewer's hello, since nothing is sent before that.
  • The learning panel. A learner's status reaches the viewer on its own port, whole in one message, and is re-sent to a viewer that attaches in the middle of a run.
  • Saving a picture or a clip to a file with no window, no display and no clock.
  • Effects, spells and shots (2026-09-24). A frozen, stunned, poisoned, slowed or raging unit wears a mark of its own. A heal or a shield gets a small sign in its corner. A spell the viewer knows is drawn in its family's shape at its card's size. A shot looks like what fired it: an arrow, a bullet or a ball. A crown tower's shot is a dot with a white core. The effect marks and the shots need a trace or a stream from an engine and a RoyaleGym of 2026-09-24 or later. With an older RoyaleGym a trace still opens, but without its shots, its targets and every effect except a stun, and nothing says so. What every mark means is in docs/internals.md.
  • Every draw redraws the whole window and takes 2-5 ms at 24 pixels per tile. A replay needs 20 a second, so that is far inside budget. That is why the viewer is Python and pygame and not a Rust program.

Known gaps. Every one of these is a source not carrying the information. None of them is the window refusing to draw something.

  • A recording gives no unit a radius and no flying flag. So every unit is drawn at one default size, and air units look like ground units.
  • A trace or a stream gives no unit a path, so the path overlay draws nothing for them. Since 2026-09-24 they do carry what each unit is attacking, so the target overlay draws. A trace saved before then, or an engine or RoyaleGym older than that, gives no targets.
  • Spells in a recording come through as projectiles, plus the few whose effect is tagged with its card (Fireball, Arrows, Rocket, Log, Barbarian Barrel). There are no rage, poison or freeze zones.
  • A recording holds only the recording player's hand. The opponent's shows as "hand: not in this source" until the results screen. A trace's cycle past the revealed cards shows as "next ?".

A clone of THIS REPO ALONE, installed the short way, runs pytest -q to 285 passed and 15 skipped (CI at adc2450, 2026-09-28, the same on Windows and Linux): the tests that need a sibling package skip and each says so. That figure is CI's, from a runner that has nothing but this repo, because this project's development machine has every sibling repo installed and cannot produce it -- measured there it gives a different pair, which is a different machine wearing the same name. CI installs the media extra as well. Without it one more test skips, so the short way on its own gives 284 passed and 16 skipped. The counts below are for a machine with the rest of the stack. Until 2026-09-23 that case could not collect the suite at all, which nothing had ever run.

Tests. Start in the Royale folder. On a clone with the media extra installed, the first line prints 369 passed, 4 skipped (2026-10-01, 500ae04). Without the extra, which Setup does not install, it prints 368 passed, 5 skipped (2026-10-01, 500ae04). The second line prints All checks passed!. Both tools come from the pip install maturin pytest hypothesis ruff numpy msgspec line in Setup, so the short way on its own does not have them:

cd RoyaleViser
..\.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q
..\.venv\Scripts\python -m ruff check royaleviser tests

Three of those skips are tests that pin numbers only a recording of a real battle has. Those recordings are private, so your clone does not have them, and the run prints "SKIPPED, NOT PASSED" for each one so nobody mistakes a skip for a pass. The fourth needs a parity results file from RoyaleSim's replay harness. On the machine that has the recordings, the first three run and the count is 372 passed, 1 skipped.

Without the media extra (imageio-ffmpeg), the mp4 and gif test skips as well, and it says so. Install it with .venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -e "RoyaleViser[media]" from the Royale folder. A PNG needs nothing extra.

Read next: docs/internals.md for the frame model, the recording format, the stream protocol, the command line, the layout, the tests and the performance table; RoyaleGym for the trace format and the sender that streams to the viewer; RoyaleSim for the engine the traces come from.

Issues and pull requests on this repo are welcome too.

docs.title: Internals
docs.text: This page is for people changing the viewer, or writing something that feeds it. The guide covers usage. Here you get the frame model, the recording format, the stream protocol, the command line, the window layout, the key table, what the viewer costs, how it is tested and what it cannot draw.

docs.title: One frame model, three sources
docs.text:
Every source produces the same royaleviser.model.Frame, so the renderer never learns where a battle came from.
